key_insight: Self-powered microsystems need a system-level energy-harvesting stack, not just better materials: ambient mechanical, thermal, and radiative sources must be paired with robust power management and storage.
engineering_relevance: The review is most relevant for designing battery-independent IoT, wearable, and cyber-physical devices by integrating harvesters, cold-start PMICs, impedance matching, and durable micro-storage.
method: Compare major harvester classes: TENGs, piezoelectric/pyroelectric devices, indoor PV, and RF rectennas.
Synthesize hybrid multi-source integration strategies for broader and more reliable ambient power capture.
Highlight enabling advances in materials discovery, nonlinear dynamics, metamaterials, and low-voltage PMIC design.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports specific performance gains such as over 300% bandwidth broadening for nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators and improved RF harvesting via metamaterial-based multiband/broadband architectures.
watch_item: Real-world deployment remains limited by ultra-low-voltage startup, source-matching complexity in hybrid systems, and degradation of micro-supercapacitors and thin-film batteries under field conditions.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
